# Designer response to the coder: kit 04 patch 1

7 September 2026. This is the authoritative revision to kit 04. Apply the supplied patch to the delivered kit, then vendor the changes into the application. The original art and recorded audio are retained. The owner’s latest cleanup request takes precedence over the earlier scene studies and placement tables.

## A. Placement and page context

**A1 — Use the existing warm shell.** Option (a): one illustrated console inside the Review tab. Keep the application nameplate, navigation and footer. Do not recolour the other tabs or add a dark page takeover. The navy is the scene’s window, not the application background. The preview surround now demonstrates the warm shell, with a dark surround under the existing dark preference.

**A2 — Keep the 1320 px cap.** This composition is now designed at that ceiling; `od-console` is capped at 1320 px. Do not widen every tab. Remove the old 360 px hero cap and old Review grid-area assignments only within the replaced console. At a console width of 1220 px or less, the two appliances stack. The source silhouettes retain their original viewBoxes.

**A3 — Remove the history drawer.** The quiet footer’s History action goes straight to the existing History tab. That tab retains paging, filters, row actions and future Run again. There is no separate last-N list, no duplicate navigation dialog and no implied new History endpoint. `history`, `runAgainAvailable` and the `run-again` action remain source-compatible types for an existing adapter, but this component no longer renders the mini-history UI.

**A4 — No invented machinery or decorative vacancies.** Absent odometer, daily-budget aggregate and Run again data produce no corresponding placeholder. There is one deliberate readout exception: after any terminal review, the existing price glass is labelled **Final review cost** and shows an em dash until a complete, numeric settlement is supplied. It must not keep showing the old estimate as though that were the final bill. Partial settlement may say **Settlement pending** in the smaller register glass. This supersedes the earlier blanket statement that all absent readouts disappear.

## B. Controls and behaviour

**B1 — Known stages are ordinal steps.** The progressbar now carries `aria-valuemin=1`, `aria-valuemax=4`, `aria-valuenow=step`, and `aria-valuetext="Step N of 4. [caption]"`. This describes the reported stage, not elapsed-time percentage. Unknown/null tokens and upload have no numeric ARIA value. The progressbar exists only while working; the toaster’s status badge describes terminal states.

**B2 — One physical lever; two plain controls.** In the illustrated surface, the one native lever button says Start or Stop according to the real state. In plain and forced-colours views, separate native **Start toaster** and **Stop review** buttons are present together, with the inapplicable action disabled. Upload disables both operations; a pending cancel shows Stopping and remains disabled until the adapter enables it after a delivery failure or supplies a terminal state. The server guards and cancellation races remain yours.

**B3 — Test ids are compatibility hooks, not visual design decisions.** Add the app’s missing hooks where needed. No hook was intentionally removed merely to shorten the list. This patch restores `review-preflight-card`, `review-cover-note-butter`, `review-receipt-paper`, `review-cost-estimate`, `review-outcome`, `notify-toggle` and intensity hooks. State-specific placement does intentionally change: completed result details exist inside the receipt overlay; disposition and cover-note fields exist inside their overlays; preflight does not exist after a terminal result. `review-status` identifies the toaster’s one status readout; `toaster-state-progress` identifies the working-only progressbar. Preserve legacy state aliases in the adapter if existing tests depend on them; do not create duplicate ids on two controls.

**B4 — Oversight, fixed.** Intensity radios now carry `review-browning-option-light`, `review-browning-option-medium`, and `review-browning-option-dark`. Footnote ids are unchanged.

**B5 — The register glass has a defined scope.** It may summarize submit, catalog, preference, cancel and poll messages; it never mirrors ordinary review state, receipt confirmation or disposition confirmation. Full error details and retry actions remain visible below the appliances when needed. Messages for the currently open receipt/review-record, cover-note or outcome overlay are rendered there. Set `Message.tone` to `success` for those local confirmations and `error` for failures. Unknown/untyped messages are kept rather than silently discarded. Do not send success confirmations as unscoped global alerts. Important errors arriving after an overlay is closed remain eligible for the main message area.

**B6 — One burnt headline.** **That one burnt.** appears once on the toaster’s status badge. A visible **What happened** panel gives the real classified cause, fix, failing stage and reason code. It is placed before the instructions pad so the next step is not buried. The register does not repeat the headline. Cancellation never uses burnt art, the clunk or this copy.

**B7 — Text plus a step number.** Forced colours retains the same Step N of 4 and caption, with a real progressbar role for assistive technology. No user needs to infer the stage from bread colour. Unknown tokens stay explicitly unreported.

## C. Copy

**C1 — Use the new cost caption with an honest basis.** Before submission: **Estimated review cost**. For the current ordinary-document estimate, the readback is: **Based on active models and typical document length. Longer documents may cost more.** For a real document/model estimate, use: **Based on this document and the active model policy.** The existing endpoint does not make the second statement true merely because preflight found a word count. Once accepted and confirmed reserved: **Review reservation** and the actual authorized hold or the word Held. After terminal status: **Final review cost**, with a number only for `kind:'settled'`, `settlementComplete:true`, and an explicit `cents` value. The extra “Actual spend is shown only…” paragraph is removed. Cover-note cost lives with the cover-note draft and remains separate.

**C2 — One cheat sheet and one keyboard owner.** Use the kit dialog as the visible cheat sheet; it now includes the four modifier/Shift chords and `?` / `Cmd/Ctrl+/`. Keep the existing app shortcut dispatcher if that minimizes integration risk, and pass `keyboardShortcuts={false}` to this component. It still owns modal Escape. The global dispatcher must return if the event was already prevented or its target is inside `dialog[open]`; capture-phase handlers must make the dialog check before acting. Do not keep two independently maintained shortcut dialogs. The documented commands are an integration contract, not a reason to remove existing supported chords.

**C3 — Final manual-review copy.** The toaster says **Needs a human**. The visible panel is titled **Next step** and shows the record’s classified explanation; if none is supplied, the adapter must provide **A person needs to review this result.** Both manual-review statuses use this treatment. Retain any classified cause/fix for an `ERROR_MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED` record without turning the scene into a burn. The ready announcement remains polite and does not steal focus.

**C4 — Use a statement the browser can prove.** **Download started automatically. Save redline repeats it.** Do not claim the file was saved to disk. This confirmation is now in the receipt overlay, not a permanent paragraph under a second download button. Actual download failures remain prominent in the main error area or open receipt, using the existing fixed storage-error copy.

## D. Art and assets

**D1 — Keep Instrument Sans 600 for keys.** The supplied 600 WOFF2 is the intended face, not synthetic bold. Reuse the app’s matching 400, Space Grotesk 500 and IBM Plex Mono 400 assets; register the included Instrument Sans 600 once. Do not register duplicate same-family faces from both the app and the vendored CSS. The adapter may redirect the four font URLs to the app’s same-origin font directory. There is no need to load 700 for these controls.

**D2 — No new phone plates in this patch.** The delivered six WebPs remain the canonical runtime set, totalling 1,491,984 bytes. Phone controls use a dedicated CSS bezel and flowing key bed, not smaller text baked into a thumbnail. No AVIF variants or srcset were previously supplied. The current silhouettes require stable source coordinates, so do not substitute a resized SVG `<image>` without retaining the original user-unit width/height. Smaller same-aspect exports can be a measured loading optimization later; they are not required to make this visual patch work. No new raster assets are introduced here.

**D3 — Keep the viewBox/aspect-ratio contract.** The clip paths and plates scale together. The toaster and register figure remain at 3:2; a narrower container changes their size or stacks them rather than stretching either one independently. The pad has fixed top and bottom skin sections, with only its middle section stretching around an untransformed native textarea; its metal clip never grows with the text. If you change a plate’s aspect ratio or crop, that would require a new silhouette and coordinate pass. Keep this patch’s container rules instead.

**D4 — Those omissions were deliberate, with one fallback refinement.** No decorative pen, stand or lower filename plate is required. The filename appears only on the toast in illustrated mode, with full text available through its accessible name/title; plain mode shows the filename once as text. Start and Stop are separate only in the plain/forced-colours layout as described in B2. The current estimate caption is C1. Browse playbooks and Save redline are now smaller physical keys in the toaster’s base. The dial is smaller and clears its surrounding label and status badge.

**D5 — The same reflective plates are intentional in dark mode.** The surrounding counter, readbacks and text treatment adapt; the material still reflects the diner’s practical lighting. No separate dark image pack is pending. Do not darken the entire composite with a filter that would also muddy text and chrome highlights.

**D6 — Keep the existing tab chrome.** Continue using your favicon frames, completion badge, document title and notification timing. Feed them from the same stage mapping as the scene. This patch has no new favicon family and introduces no title timer.

## E. Sound

**E1 — Deployment choice; original pop is the default.** A deployment config may select `completion:'register'`; do not add a new stored user preference or play both loud identities. Preserve the existing failure clunk in the app’s central sound owner. If using the supplied bus intact, its failure route pitches a supplied raw recording to 0.72 playback rate; point that route at the original lever recording, not at an already processed clunk. If your existing owner already plays the processed failure sound, leave the bus failure URL unconfigured and integrate the new recorded hiss into that one owner. Never double-trigger the old and new handlers. The 19 recorded effects and all source provenance remain unchanged.

**E2 — Keep the existing tick when sound is enabled.** Keep the existing approximately 446 ms trigger and recorded tick. Stage cues are finite one-shots when a genuinely new backend stage arrives. Duck the tick to 12% of its normal gain over 20 ms; restore over 120 ms after the last one-shot. One central voice budget is three, including the tick. The kit preview still has no running tick because the original recording is not in this package. No sound rhythm changes review progress.

**E3 — A default only fills an absent preference.** Respect every existing stored mute value, including an explicit unmuted value from a reviewer who prefers reduced motion. Only if there is no stored value does reduced motion choose the default mute state. Mute changes stop sound immediately. Hidden-tab browser notifications stay silent while muted; permission is requested only on the explicit Browser alerts gesture.

## F. Accessibility and fallbacks

**F1 — Blocking defects corrected in code and new renders.** Forced colours automatically selects the plain layout; every decorative SVG, including `SmallArt`, is hidden. The select, textarea, receipt and action keys have two-pixel system-colour borders; checked radios also have an explicit Highlight border. The empty dial is gone, and Start/Stop become native separate buttons. The layout uses Canvas, CanvasText, ButtonFace, ButtonText, GrayText and Highlight without fixed cream gradients or red decorative type. The patch includes fresh Chromium forced-colours captures. Actual Windows/browser/assistive-technology acceptance remains an app-level gate, not something a jsdom test proves.

**F2 — Expose a real plain-controls escape hatch.** The component now supplies a quiet footer toggle. Its default implementation is session-only React state, with no new storage call. `plain` and optional `onPlainChange` allow the app to own it. Persisting a new preference is not authorized by the current enumerated storage contract; a future approved server preference can use that callback. Forced colours always takes precedence and disables return to the illustration while active. It is not merely a preview switch.

**F3 — 44 × 44 CSS px is the minimum interaction box.** This applies to service keys, radios, Browse, intake actions and download, including the 320 px layout. The new phone till uses two columns; its final Shortcuts key spans the row. The toaster’s lower keys extend into an attached base rail instead of shrinking inside the image. Font size stays at least 14 px. The browser verification includes target dimensions, not just a CSS source guard.

**F4 — One active modal, predictable Escape and focus.** The shared native dialog now hosts receipt, playbooks, cover note, outcome, review-record and shortcuts content; history navigates directly. Escape inside closes the current dialog, prevents the default and stops propagation. Focus returns to the invoking control; opening does not move focus out of another open modal. The app’s global dispatcher must ignore open-dialog targets even for modifier chords. Outside dialogs, input/textarea/select/contenteditable guards remain; Escape must not eject while typing. Normal completion never automatically opens a modal or moves focus. A terminal result is inspected only after a user action.

## G. Delivery

**G1 — Vendor the source.** Keep a readable vendored directory rather than introducing a package registry dependency. This delivery is `04 → 04p1`, version `0.4.1`, against the exact delivered kit bytes. The ZIP contains changed files only, a unified source diff, verification captures, a baseline-aware apply helper and hashes. Apply to `frontend/orbit-diner-kit-04` if that directory still matches kit 04; if you have already vendored or edited the source, merge the source diff into that copy. Do not replace the application’s guarded handlers with preview fixtures.

**G2 — The patch has an exact changelog against kit 04.** `CHANGELOG-04p1.md` maps the owner’s requests to the implemented changes. Study 02 is not the patch baseline. At the design level, the later kit moved from study mockups to native React controls, arbitrary-size playbook browsing, functional receipt export, a growing native pad, all 22 action surfaces and the recorded sound pack. I am not claiming an exact source diff against a study archive that was not the verified baseline for this delivery.

**G3 — Per-plate provenance is now supplied.** See `ART-PROVENANCE-04p1.json` and the appended notices. Each entry identifies the generated material plate, master and WebP hashes, dimensions, supplied reference and deterministic export step. The generator was OpenAI image generation through the conversation’s image-generation tool; the original record does not supply an exact underlying model revision or reproducible seed, and the manifest does not invent one. OpenAI’s applicable business agreement assigns its rights, if any, in output to the customer and notes that output may not be unique. This does not make the plates CC0 or choose an open-source licence for your repository. Keep the generated-art notice distinct from the CC0 recording notices. [OpenAI Services Agreement, sections 4.1–4.4](https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/).

## Automatic playbook choice requested by the owner

The dial is a view of the selected playbook, so any accepted automatic choice moves it immediately. The source now exports `preflightPlaybookChoice`, a pure adapter helper. Supply a unique in-memory file key for each selection/replacement and the key captured by the preflight request. Apply a recommendation only when classification is available/ok, the request belongs to the current file, the recommended playbook is active, review submission has not started, and the reviewer has not manually overridden the selection for that file. Set `userOverride=true` on any dial, select, browse-list or explicit recommendation action; reset it for a genuinely new document. A late response cannot reverse the override or alter an in-flight request. An initial/default or previously saved choice is not automatically a manual override for a newly selected file.

The helper makes no model call and invents no confidence threshold. The adapter supplies the active recommended id from its existing trusted preflight/classification mapping. If it cannot resolve a usable recommendation, keep the current selection and the advisory warning/switch action. Set the optional `playbookSelection:'automatic'|'user'` projection so the browse overlay can explain the choice. No new browser storage is involved.
